newsitem.title: USA: Boeing Co plans for the 757-300 progress.
newsitem.headline: Boeing Co plans for the 757-300 progress.

text.p: Boeing Co said Friday it is closer to building its planned 757-300 aircraft, the company's latest single-aisle airplane.
Boeing said in a statement it had agreed on the configuration on the new aircraft with its customers keeping it on track for a first delivery date of January 1999.

The new plane will be a stretch version of the existing 757-200. The aircraft will be a little over 23 feet longer than the 757-200, will carry 20 percent more passengers and hold 50 percent more cargo.
Because of the extra length Boeing had to make alterations to the wings, landing gear and other aspects of the existing model. The 757-300 will fly 4,000 statute miles.
Boeing launched the new model in September at the Farnborough Air Show in England. The first firm order for the aircraft is from German holiday airline Condor Flugdienst.
